item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers.
item.description:
Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers.

Dončić put on a show Sunday night, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line as part of an elite stat line. With the Lakers’ deep reserves failing to put the Raptors away, head coach JJ Redick had to insert four starters back into the game. That got Dončić four more points from the foul line. The lone negative was the seven turnovers, but the stat line was so robust that few will complain. The Lakers play four games next week, starting with the Heat on Monday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Derrick Jones (LAC): Derrick Jones Jr. (knee) finished Sunday’s loss to the Warriors with nine points (3-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer.
item.description:
Derrick Jones Jr. (knee) finished Sunday’s loss to the Warriors with nine points (3-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer.

Jones exited Sunday’s game late in the third quarter with a sore knee and did not return. That casts some doubt on his availability for Monday’s game against the Raptors. If Jones can’t play, Kobe Sanders may move into the starting lineup.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: Ohm Youngmisuk

item.title: [Injury] Gui Santos (GSW): Gui Santos (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns.
item.description:
Gui Santos (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns.

Santos did not play in the second half of Sunday’s win over the Clippers, finishing with four points, three rebounds, one assist and one block in nine minutes. Following the victory, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr said that the team will re-evaluate Santos, whose knee tendinitis remains an issue. At a minimum, he’ll miss Monday’s game, which could mean more playing time for Georges Niang

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Immanuel Quickley (TOR): Immanuel Quickley accounted for 12 points (3-of-13 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Immanuel Quickley accounted for 12 points (3-of-13 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.

Quickley has made at least three three-pointers in four straight and five of six games this season. That, along with the rebounds and assists, was the positive from his performance on Sunday. However, Quickley shot poorly against the Lakers, dropping his field-goal percentage to 37.6 percent for the season. It certainly isn’t impossible for a guard to provide solid value despite a low field-goal percentage, but fantasy managers want to see Quickley shoot better than he has.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] RJ Barrett (TOR): RJ Barrett accumulated 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), 10 rebounds, five assists and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
RJ Barrett accumulated 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), 10 rebounds, five assists and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers.

Barrett has scored at least 20 points in three of his last four games, a stretch that coincides with the Raptors’ loss of Kawhi Leonard to a knee injury. While he didn’t record any defensive stats on Sunday, fantasy managers will be pleased with Barrett’s double-double, his first of the season, and the assists. The Raptors play three games next week, starting with the Clippers on Monday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Scottie Barnes (TOR): Scottie Barnes finished Sunday’s loss to the Lakers with 29 points (11-of-20 FGs, 7-of-13 FTs), six rebounds, five assists and two steals.
item.description:
Scottie Barnes finished Sunday’s loss to the Lakers with 29 points (11-of-20 FGs, 7-of-13 FTs), six rebounds, five assists and two steals.

Barnes’ mid-range mastery helped him score 29 points, and he’s scored at least 28 in three straight and four of his last five games. The exception was the October 25 loss to the Timberwolves, in which the Raptors’ star went scoreless. With Kawhi Leonard (knee) out for a few weeks, Barnes will need to shoulder more responsibility on both ends of the floor. And he’s shown the ability to do that in the past.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Walker Kessler (LAL): Walker Kessler amassed 16 points (6-of-6 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 15 rebounds, one assist, one steal and three blocks in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
item.description:
Walker Kessler amassed 16 points (6-of-6 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 15 rebounds, one assist, one steal and three blocks in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.

A favorite of many fantasy managers willing to punt free-throw percentage, Kessler didn’t miss a shot from the field or the foul line on Sunday. Add in the rebounds and blocks, and this was a nice end to the week for those rostering the 7-footer. Kessler, who’s averaging just under three blocks per game, has blocked at least three shots in three games.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Austin Reaves (LAL): Austin Reaves tallied 19 points (6-of-16 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
item.description:
Austin Reaves tallied 19 points (6-of-16 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.

After committing eight turnovers in Friday’s loss to the Warriors, Reaves committed three against the Raptors. He didn’t shoot the ball particularly well on Sunday, but Reaves entered the game shooting 54.8 percent from the field and 42.4 percent from beyond the arc. He’ll look to bounce back on Monday when the Lakers host the Heat.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers.
item.description:
Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers.

Dončić put on a show Sunday night, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line as part of an elite stat line. With the Lakers’ deep reserves failing to put the Raptors away, head coach JJ Redick had to insert four starters back into the game. That got Dončić four more points from the foul line. The lone negative was the seven turnovers, but the stat line was so robust that few will complain. The Lakers play four games next week, starting with the Heat on Monday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kris Dunn (LAC): Kris Dunn accumulated 12 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists and seven steals in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Kris Dunn accumulated 12 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists and seven steals in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.

After failing to record a steal in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves, Dunn compensated with the best performance of his career. The seven steals mark a new career high for the former lottery pick, whose defense has made him a fixture in Tyronn Lue’s rotation since he joined the Clippers in 2024-25. Dunn also shot well on Sunday, but his defensive potential makes him an intriguing option for managers in 12-team leagues seeking steals.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kobe Sanders (LAC): Kobe Sanders amassed 16 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Kobe Sanders amassed 16 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.

Sanders had his most productive game of the season so far, setting new highs in points and three-pointers. He’s now played at least 20 minutes in four straight games, logging 30 against the Warriors. Sunday’s performance isn’t enough to get him on the radar in most fantasy leagues, but it may ensure Sanders a place in head coach Tyronn Lue’s rotation while the Clippers await the returns of Brandon Ingram and Max Strus.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Kingston Flemings (ATL): Kingston Flemings has been suspended one game for his actions during Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans.
item.description:
Kingston Flemings has been suspended one game for his actions during Saturday’s loss to the Pelicans.

Flemings was ejected from Saturday’s game after elbowing Pelicans wing Bryce McGowens in the face during a confrontation. The NBA has since suspended the rookie for one game, which he’ll serve on Monday against the Pacers. Flemings will be eligible to return on Wednesday against the Wizards.

Raphielle Johnson

Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is out for Sunday’s game against the Lakers.

item.title: [Recap] Andrew Nembhard (IND): Andrew Nembhard finished Sunday’s loss to the Nets with 23 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers.
item.description:
Andrew Nembhard finished Sunday’s loss to the Nets with 23 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers.

Nembhard has scored at least 18 points in each of his last three games, all played without Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring). However, his efficiency has taken a hit, with Nembhard shooting 39.2 percent from the field and recording nine turnovers in those three outings. He’ll look to clean that up on Monday when the Pacers host the Hawks to begin a three-game week.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jay Huff (IND): Jay Huff missed both of his shot attempts in Sunday’s loss to the Nets, finishing with zero points and three rebounds.
item.description:
Jay Huff missed both of his shot attempts in Sunday’s loss to the Nets, finishing with zero points and three rebounds.

It’s fair to say that Huff’s four starts for the injured Ivica Zubac (ankle) have not gone as well as many fantasy managers hoped. While he scored 13 points in Friday’s loss to the Heat, he has totaled 22 points, 16 rebounds and one block in those four games. Huff appeared to tweak his right foot in the first half of Sunday’s defeat but returned. Managers still holding onto him in hopes of getting some streaming value may be best served by moving on to another option going into Week 3.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Pascal Siakam (IND): Pascal Siakam tallied 17 points (6-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and one steal in Sunday’s loss to the Nets.
item.description:
Pascal Siakam tallied 17 points (6-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and one steal in Sunday’s loss to the Nets.

In the three games the Pacers have played since losing Tyrese Haliburton to a hamstring strain, Siakam has averaged 18.7 points per game while shooting 45.8 percent from the field. That isn’t necessarily bad, but not sharing the floor with a lead guard as talented as Haliburton lowers Siakam’s ceiling. On Sunday, he scored just four points in the second half, shooting 1-of-3 from the field. The Pacers play three games next week, starting with the Hawks on Monday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Nolan Traore (BKN): Nolan Traoré accounted for 16 points (6-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, six assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
item.description:
Nolan Traoré accounted for 16 points (6-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, six assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.

Having started the Nets’ last three games, Traoré’s production has been inconsistent. He rebounded nicely from a poor outing against the Pistons on Friday, scoring in double figures for the third time in four games. Traoré shot 4-of-8 from beyond the arc and committed one turnover in 30 minutes. Monday’s matchup against the Knicks will be more challenging, and Mikel Brown Jr. (back) should be available, which may limit Traoré’s ceiling.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Day'Ron Sharpe (BKN): Day’Ron Sharpe amassed 15 points (5-of-7 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
item.description:
Day’Ron Sharpe amassed 15 points (5-of-7 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.

Playing against a Pacers team without Ivica Zubac or Obi Toppin, Sharpe had his most productive game of the season. The Nets center recorded his first double-double in six games, finishing with new highs in points and rebounds. Sharpe didn’t record any defensive stats, ending his two-game streak with at least one steal and one block. He’ll look to do more on that end of the floor on Monday when the Nets visit the Knicks.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Julius Randle (BKN): Julius Randle recorded 20 points (5-of-15 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
item.description:
Julius Randle recorded 20 points (5-of-15 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.

Despite shooting 1-of-6 from inside the arc, Randle finished Sunday’s victory with his third 20-point game of the season. Unfortunately for category league managers, Randle wasn’t efficient, shooting 33.3 percent from the field and committing four turnovers. That said, his performance against the Pacers was better than Friday’s showing against the Pistons.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Michael Porter (BKN): Michael Porter Jr. tallied 23 points (7-of-16 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
item.description:
Michael Porter Jr. tallied 23 points (7-of-16 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.

The Nets got their first win of the season on Sunday, and getting Porter involved early helped. The Nets forward scored seven points in the first quarter and 13 in the first half. After attempting nine shots in Friday’s loss to the Pistons, Porter nearly matched that number in the first quarter (seven). He’ll need to take a similar approach on Monday when the Nets begin a four-game week with a matchup with the Knicks.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Gui Santos (GSW): Gui Santos (knee) is available for Sunday’s game against the Clippers.
item.description:
Gui Santos (knee) is available for Sunday’s game against the Clippers.

Santos is good to go after being listed as probable on the initial injury report. While he may start, it isn’t guaranteed that Santos will get the minutes needed to affect fantasy basketball. He most recently played 16 minutes in Friday’s win over the Lakers.

item.title: [Injury] Ziaire Williams (LAL): Lakers head coach JJ Redick said Sunday that Ziaire Williams (foot) is dealing with soreness, so he’s sitting out Sunday’s game against the Raptors.
item.description:
Lakers head coach JJ Redick said Sunday that Ziaire Williams (foot) is dealing with soreness, so he’s sitting out Sunday’s game against the Raptors.

Sunday’s game will be the third Williams has missed due to left foot/heel injury management. The good news is that, while Williams is dealing with soreness, scans of the foot came back clean. Jake LaRavia should remain in the starting lineup until Williams is cleared to return.

Raphielle Johnson

item.description:
Zach LaVine (elbow) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Mavericks.

LaVine is dealing with right elbow inflammation. He hasn’t missed a game this season, but if that changes, Malik Monk could take on a bigger role, whether he starts or comes off the bench.

item.description:
Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) is doubtful for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.

Pippen did not play in Saturday’s win over the Kings and appears likely to remain out on Monday. Ty Jerome (back) is available, so Pippen remaining out would not put the Grizzlies in a terrible spot. Javon Small could play some off the bench after logging 20 minutes on Saturday, but that isn’t guaranteed.

item.description:
Ty Jerome (back) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Pelicans.

item.title: [Recap] Franz Wagner (ORL): Franz Wagner tallied 14 points (5-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, 12 assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
item.description:
Franz Wagner tallied 14 points (5-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, 12 assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.

While Wagner set a career high with 12 assists, he struggled to make shots. Shooting 54.2 percent from inside the arc entering Sunday, the Magic forward shot 4-of-16 from inside the arc against the Celtics. Wagner is shooting 39.6 percent for the season, but three-point shooting has been the issue (18.5 percent entering Sunday). He’ll look to turn things around on Monday against the Wizards.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Anthony Black (ORL): Anthony Black recorded 23 points (6-of-12 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
item.description:
Anthony Black recorded 23 points (6-of-12 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.

Black has reached double figures in three of his four games this season, and Sunday’s point total is a new season-high. The overall stat line was very good, with the Magic guard shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line and offering solid value in rebounds and steals. Black will continue to start until Paolo Banchero (ankle) returns, making him worth adding if he’s still on your league’s waiver wire.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Desmond Bane (ORL): Desmond Bane accumulated 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
item.description:
Desmond Bane accumulated 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.

For the second straight game, Bane made at least five three-pointers, shooting 5-of-9 against the Celtics. The Magic guard shot over 50 percent from the field on Sunday, a sign he’s warming up after a slow start. Bane is shooting 36.9 percent from the field through six games, far below his career mark of 47.3 percent. Orlando begins a three-game Week 3 on Monday against the Wizards.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Neemias Queta (BOS): Neemias Queta produced eight points (4-of-9 FGs), nine rebounds, one assist and two blocks in Sunday’s win over the Magic.
item.description:
Neemias Queta produced eight points (4-of-9 FGs), nine rebounds, one assist and two blocks in Sunday’s win over the Magic.

Mitchell Robinson (rest) did not play in the first game of Boston’s road back-to-back, so Queta started at center. While he didn’t offer much scoring, the 7-footer was effective on the glass and as a rim protector. On offense, the Celtics got solid contributions from Luka Garza, who finished with 10 points, two rebounds, one assist, and two three-pointers. Boston visits Houston on Monday, and Robinson should return to the starting lineup.

Raphielle Johnson

item.description:
Alex Caruso (ankle) is out for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers.

Monday’s game will be the third that Caruso has missed since spraining his right ankle during Oklahoma City’s October 26 win over the Suns. Injuries have forced the Thunder to go deep into their bench, with rookie Bennett Stirtz playing 25 minutes or more in each of the last three games.

Isaiah Joe (hip) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Hornets.

item.title: [Injury] LeBron James (PHI): LeBron James (sciatica) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Bulls.
item.description:
LeBron James (sciatica) is not on the injury report for Monday’s game against the Bulls.

LeBron is back after missing Saturday’s win over the Hornets, the second game of a back-to-back. Who he pushes to the bench may depend on Joel Embiid (foot), who is questionable. If Embiid can play, Dean Wade would head to the bench. If Embiid can’t play, the 76ers could go without a true center, starting LeBron and Wade together, with Adem Bona on the bench.

item.title: [Injury] Tobias Harris (SAS): Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said Saturday that the team is being “very, very methodical” in the handling of Tobias Harris’ (calf) rehab.
item.description:
Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said Saturday that the team is being “very, very methodical” in the handling of Tobias Harris’ (calf) rehab.

Harris, whom the Spurs signed to a two-year deal in July, has not yet played because of a strained calf suffered during training camp. Based on Johnson’s pregame comments on Saturday, the veteran forward may not take the court for some time. “We need to just be patient and make sure we get it all the way right and get him all the way right in terms of being ready to prepare to play an NBA game at the (fast-paced) style of play we want,” Johnson said. Until then, the Spurs may not make any changes to their starting lineup as long as the current starters are healthy.

item.description:

The Warriors got off to a terribly slow start, being outscored 38-15 in the first quarter.
